newsitem.title: USA: GTE earnings in line, revenue growth hits 5-yr high. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: GTE earnings in line, revenue growth hits 5-yr high. [CORRECTED 20:45 GMT]

text.p: GTE Corp second quarter earnings were in line with Wall Street's consensus after charges for an acquisition and data network investments, but revenue growth swelled past analysts' expectations.

GTE, a U.S. local phone giant with significant cellular holdings and a fast-growing long distance business, said revenue growth hit a five-year high during the second quarter. Revenues rose 7.5 percent to $5.69 billion.
Net income was in line with Wall Street consensus expectations of $671 million, or $0.70 per share, which included a $0.03 per share charge for new data investments.
"I am particularly pleased with top-line growth of 7.5 percent," Charles Lee, GTE's chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.

"These results not only reflect the strength of our markets, but also our ability to respond to our customers with new and expanded service offerings, such as long distance, and to bundle them together on a single bill," he said.

GTE, which marketing long distance services largely to its local service customer base in March 1996, said it had 1.3 million long distance customers at the close of the second quarter, a one million customer increase since June 30, 1996.

During the second quarter, GTE acquired Internet service provider BBN Corp for about $616 million, purchased vast new additional fiber optic capacity from Qwest Communications International Inc and forged a strategic alliance with data networking giant Cisco Systems Inc.
These data initiatives were designed to enable GTE to become a national supplier of integrated voice and data telecommunications services, the company said.
GTE said it sustained solid growth of 1.6 million access lines, or 8 percent year-to-year. It said it had 25 percent more customers ordering second phone lines than a year ago.
It said minutes of use of its U.S. local-exchange network for long distance calls grew 14 percent to 19.7 billion minutes.

New service revenues rose $198 million to $467 million, (corrects from "rose to $198 million") year-to-year, a 74 percent rise, driven by long distance, data and video services, Chief Finance Officer Mike Kelly said in an interiew.
The company said its domestic cellular customer base grew 28 percent, adding 903,000 new customers in the last 12 months, and 137,000 new customers since the first quarter.
U.S. cellular revenues totaled $654 million in the second quarter, up $67 million or 11 percent versus a year ago.

Revenues from domestic network services, which include GTE's wireline and wireless operations, increased $243 million, or 7 percent to $3.65 billion for the second quarter, compared to $3.41 billion in the year-ago quarter.

For the quarter, revenues per subscriber averaged $53, equal to the first quarter of 1997, but lower than the second quarter of 1996, which was $62, reflecting the impact of competitive promotions and pricing plans, the company said.
It said customer turnover rates improved 17 percent from the same period last year and 30 percent from the fourth quarter of 1995.

Directory services revenues declined 6.8 percent to $372 million in the second quarter due to the timing of publication of new directories and an unusually strong publishing cycle in the year ago quarter, Kelly said.
International operations grew 6 percent, Lee said.
GTE's consolidated operating income grew 7 percent to $1.44 billion, excluding the effects associated with the recently announced data initiatives.

Reported operating income grew 5 percent to $1.41 billion, compared to $1.34 billion in 1996, primarily the result of the continued growth in GTE's core wireline and wireless revenues and ongoing operating cost-reduction programs.

Partially offsetting these improvements were costs associated with the recently announced data initiatives, higher selling and marketing expenses associated with the growth in wireless and long-distance customers, the launch of PCS services and increased video activities.

Montgomery Securities analyst Bill Vogel said GTE's earnings were right on target with his estimates but that top line revenue growth of 7.5 percent in the quarter was well above his 6.4 percent projection.
He attributed the upside in revenues to incremental revenue from long distance services that are boosting the total bill GTE receives from its local service customers.
"That's all year over year goodneess," Vogel said of the additional long distance revenues.
"They are just aiming the torpedoes and going full speed ahead in terms of the core business," he said.
-- Eric Auchard, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1712
